Clip an rij matrix to an area of interest

Source: R/rij.R
clip_rij_matrix.Rd

Keeps the columns of an rij matrix that fall in an area of interest (AOI), so national data read with read_rij_matrix() can be turned into rasters for the AOI only. An rij matrix is a sparse matrix of feature values: one row per feature (i), one column per template cell with data (j, a planning unit in prioritizr's terms), as made by prioritizr::rij_matrix(). By default, rows (features) with no values in the AOI are dropped, and a message names them.

Usage

clip_rij_matrix(rij, aoi_raster, template, drop_empty = TRUE)

Arguments

rij

The rij matrix: a Matrix::dgCMatrix with unique row names and one column per template cell with data, in terra's cell order, as read_rij_matrix() returns.

aoi_raster

The AOI as a raster: a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file, on the template's grid (same CRS, resolution and cell origin). Its extent may be the template's full extent or any part of it, such as the cropped raster rasterize_aoi() returns. Every cell that is not NA is in the AOI, whatever its value.

template

The template raster the rij matrix was built on: a SpatRaster with one layer and a CRS, or a path to a raster file. Only which of its cells have data (are not NA) is used, not its values.

drop_empty

A single logical. TRUE (the default) drops rows with no values in the AOI (every value 0 or NA) and names them in a message; wtw-data-prep2 dropped them silently. FALSE keeps every row.

Value

A sparse matrix (Matrix::dgCMatrix) with the kept rows of rij, named, and one column per AOI cell with template data, in terra's cell order, without column names. With no such cells it has no columns (and, with drop_empty = TRUE, no rows).

Method

  • AOI cells: the cells of aoi_raster that are not NA, matched to the template's cells by position on the shared grid (whole row and column offsets from the template's top-left cell), with no resampling or reprojection. AOI cells outside the template's extent, or where the template is NA, have no column in rij and are left out.

  • Columns: the template's cells with data are counted in terra's cell order (row by row from the top-left cell) to find each AOI cell's column in rij; the template is read in blocks of rows, so a national template is not held in memory whole. rij is subset to those columns, keeping their order; nothing is bound to rij first, so a large matrix is not copied whole.

  • Rows (drop_empty = TRUE): a row is kept if at least one of its values in the AOI is neither 0 nor NA; negative values count. Kept rows keep their order.

  • Values are not changed: no rounding, no areas.

Method choices are recorded in ADR 0012.

See also

rasterize_aoi() to make aoi_raster.

Other rij: extract_layers(), read_rij_matrix(), rij_matrix_to_raster()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
rij <- read_rij_matrix(
  system.file("extdata", "rij.rds", package = "constechr"),
  template
)
dim(rij)
#> [1]  3 96

# The AOI's cells on the template: cells 34 35 36 44 45 46 54 55 56
aoi_raster <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")

# One column per AOI cell; sp_b has no values in the AOI, so it is dropped
x <- clip_rij_matrix(rij, aoi_raster, template)
#> Dropped 1 row of `rij` with no values in the AOI: "sp_b".
as.matrix(x)
#>       [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8] [,9]
#> sp_a     1    1    0    0  1.0    1    0    0    1
#> cover    0    0    0    0  1.6    0    0    0    0

# Keep every row
dim(clip_rij_matrix(rij, aoi_raster, template, drop_empty = FALSE))
#> [1] 3 9
